instrument_name: IRS Publication 15-A (2026) Employer's Supplemental Tax Guide - statutory employees
article_or_section: Statutory employees (four categories; income tax; reporting)
figure_or_rule_carried: Statutory employees: (1) agent/commission driver distributing beverages other than milk, meat, vegetables, fruit, bakery products or laundry/dry cleaning; (2) full-time life insurance sales agent; (3) at-home worker on supplied materials with specifications; (4) full-time traveling/city salesperson taking orders from wholesalers/retailers etc. Social security and Medicare taxes withheld when the three conditions are met; "Don't withhold federal income tax from the wages of statutory employees"; W-2 box 13 "Statutory employee", pay in box 1 as other compensation, boxes 3-6 carry FICA. FUTA applies to categories 1 and 4 only.

instrument_name: IRS Publication 15 (2026) farmwork tests and Form 943; IRS About Pub. 51 (discontinued)
article_or_section: Farmwork $150/$2,500 tests; Form 943; FUTA farmworkers test; about-publication-51 Recent developments
figure_or_rule_carried: Cash wages to a farmworker of $150 or more in a year, OR total farmwork pay (cash and non-cash) to all employees of $2,500 or more in the year, make cash wages subject to social security, Medicare and income tax withholding; seasonal farmworker below $150 excepted. FUTA farmworkers test 2026: cash wages $20,000 or more in any calendar quarter of 2025 or 2026, or 10 or more farmworkers on some part of a day in 20 or more different weeks. Agricultural employers report on Form 943. Pub. 51 "will no longer be revised -- 23-JAN-2024" (IRS about page); content moved to Pub. 15 (closes the Pub. 51 404 gap).

instrument_name: IRS Publication 54 (12/2025) Tax Guide for U.S. Citizens and Resident Aliens Abroad - employer withholding and social security abroad
article_or_section: Employer withholding / Form 673; Social Security and Medicare Taxes: American employer, foreign affiliate
figure_or_rule_carried: Full page text read (about 305,000 characters). Employer may stop withholding once a U.S.-citizen employee submits a statement under penalties of perjury that they expect to qualify for the foreign earned income or housing exclusion (Form 673 acceptable, citizens only); "if your employer has reason to believe that you will not qualify ... your employer must continue to withhold". U.S. social security and Medicare tax applies abroad when working for an American employer or, by Form 2032 agreement, a foreign affiliate; totalization agreements exempt dual coverage. Inflation-adjusted amounts (incl. FEIE) were REMOVED from the publication; they come from the Rev. Proc. (US-FED-025). A WebFetch summary of this page wrongly said employers "may not withhold"; corrected from the local text.
